es: Organizar una propuesta en problema, evidencia, solución y resultado esperado con conectores claros.

teaching.en: The problem is that the empty space behind the library has no shade.
teaching.es: El problema es que el espacio vacío detrás de la biblioteca no tiene sombra.
teaching.explanationEs: The problem is that + oración presenta lo que falla ahora.
segments: The problem is that the empty space
behind the library has no shade.
teaching.audioText: The problem is that the empty space behind the library has no shade.

teaching.en: For example, families leave after ten minutes because there are no seats.
teaching.es: Por ejemplo, las familias se van a los diez minutos porque no hay asientos.
teaching.explanationEs: For example + dato da la prueba; because da la razón.
segments: For example, families leave after ten
minutes because there are no seats.
teaching.audioText: For example, families leave after ten minutes because there are no seats.

teaching.en: So we propose a small garden with benches and trees.
teaching.es: Así que proponemos un pequeño jardín con bancos y árboles.
teaching.explanationEs: So + we propose: la solución responde al problema.
segments: So we propose a small
garden with benches and trees.
teaching.audioText: So we propose a small garden with benches and trees.

teaching.en: As a result, more families may stay and read.
teaching.es: Como resultado, más familias pueden quedarse a leer.
teaching.explanationEs: As a result + may: lo esperado, sin prometerlo.
segments: As a result, more families
may stay and read.
teaching.audioText: As a result, more families may stay and read.

teaching.en: The proposal has four parts: the problem, the evidence, the solution and the result.
teaching.es: La propuesta tiene cuatro partes: el problema, la prueba, la solución y el resultado.
teaching.explanationEs: Esta es la estructura y siempre va en este orden.
segments: The proposal has four parts: the problem,
the evidence, the solution and the result.
teaching.audioText: The proposal has four parts: the problem, the evidence, the solution and the result.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase presenta la solución para este problema?

choices.text: Because we propose a reading garden.
For example, we propose a reading garden.
So we propose a reading garden.

feedback.es: La solución responde al problema y se abre con «So we propose». Because da una razón y for example da un dato.

hint.es: La solución responde al problema: busca el conector del «así que».

origin.text: The problem is that children have no quiet place to read near the library.

prompt.es: Completa: «Las familias se van pronto porque no hay asientos.»

answer.text: because

feedback.es: Because introduce la razón de lo que acaba de decirse: no hay asientos.

hint.es: Introduce una razón, no un resultado.

origin.text: Families leave early ___ there are no seats.

prompt.es: Ordena el resultado: «Como resultado, más familias pueden quedarse.»

answer.text: As a result more families may stay

feedback.es: El resultado esperado abre con as a result y usa may para no prometer.

hint.es: Empieza con el conector del resultado.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase es una evidencia y no una solución?

choices.text: For example, ten families left before noon.
So we propose a reading garden.
As a result, more families may stay.

feedback.es: La evidencia es un dato real y se abre con for example. Las otras dos frases son la solución y el resultado.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada conector con lo que introduce.

feedback.es: Cada conector marca una parte distinta de la propuesta, en este orden.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige la solución que propone el texto.

choices.text: benches
trees
a new library

feedback.es: Después de «So we propose» el audio nombra la solución: trees. Shade y seats son los problemas.

origin.audio: The library has no shade and no seats. So we propose trees.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase une bien el problema y la solución?

choices.text: Many bikes stay in the shed, because we propose a free repair corner.
Many bikes stay in the shed, for example we propose a free repair corner.
Many bikes stay in the shed, so we propose a free repair corner.

feedback.es: Para pasar del problema a la solución se usa so. Because y for example cambian el sentido de la frase.

origin.text: Problem: many bikes stay in the school shed. Solution: a free repair corner.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige el dato que el texto da como evidencia.

choices.text: Last month, more than ten bikes stayed in the shed.
Last month, fewer than ten bikes stayed in the shed.
Last year, more than ten bikes stayed in the shed.

feedback.es: Tras «For example» el audio da el dato: sixteen bikes, last month; dieciséis es más de diez. Otras opciones cambian la cantidad o el tiempo.

origin.audio: The problem is that many bikes are broken. For example, sixteen bikes stayed in the shed last month.

prompt.es: Completa: «Por eso proponemos un rincón de reparaciones gratis los sábados.»

answer.text: propose

feedback.es: Propose es el verbo de la solución: we propose + la acción.

origin.text: So we ___ a free repair corner on Saturdays.

prompt.es: Escribe el resultado esperado de la propuesta sin prometerlo.

answer.text: As a result, there may be fewer broken bikes in the shed.
accepted: As a result, there may be fewer broken bikes in the shed.
As a result there may be fewer broken bikes in the shed.
As a result, fewer bikes may be broken in the shed.
As a result, there may be fewer broken bikes in the school shed.

feedback.es: El resultado se abre con as a result y usa may: es lo esperado, no una garantía.

origin.text: Solución: un rincón de reparaciones gratis. Resultado esperado: menos bicis rotas en el cobertizo.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase dice el resultado esperado sin prometerlo?

choices.text: As a result, families will spend nothing on clothes.
As a result, families may spend less on clothes.
For example, families may spend less on clothes.

feedback.es: Con as a result + may se expresa lo esperado. Will promete de más y for example no introduce un resultado.

prompt.es: Ordena la solución: «Así que proponemos un día de intercambio de ropa.»

answer.text: So we propose a clothes swap day

feedback.es: La solución se abre con so we propose y nombra la acción: un día de intercambio.

prompt.es: Completa: «Los niños crecen rápido, así que se compra ropa nueva cada temporada.»

answer.text: so

feedback.es: So une la causa (crecen rápido) con la consecuencia (compran ropa nueva).

origin.text: Children grow fast, ___ families buy new clothes every season.

es: Comprender las posturas, los puntos en común y las condiciones de tres participantes en una reunión.

teaching.en: Sara will support the garden because families need a quiet place.
teaching.es: Sara apoyará el jardín porque las familias necesitan un lugar tranquilo.
teaching.explanationEs: Support + nombre: apoyar una idea. Because da la razón.
segments: Sara will support the garden because
families need a quiet place.
teaching.audioText: Sara will support the garden because families need a quiet place.

teaching.en: Carlos will agree, but only if the council has a safety plan; that is his condition.
teaching.es: Carlos estará de acuerdo, pero solo si el ayuntamiento tiene un plan de seguridad: esa es su condición.
teaching.explanationEs: Only if marca una condición necesaria; después va presente.
segments: Carlos will agree, but only if the council
has a safety plan; that is his condition.
teaching.audioText: Carlos will agree, but only if the council has a safety plan; that is his condition.

teaching.en: Tom says, "I disagree, because I worry that the garden will be noisy."
teaching.es: Tom dice: «No estoy de acuerdo, porque me preocupa que el jardín sea ruidoso.»
teaching.explanationEs: I disagree: no estoy de acuerdo. Worry that + oración: lo que preocupa.
segments: Tom says, "I disagree, because I worry
that the garden will be noisy."
teaching.audioText: Tom says, "I disagree, because I worry that the garden will be noisy."

segments: Tom will support the garden as

teaching.audioText: Tom will support the garden as long as it closes at six.

teaching.en: Everyone agrees that families need a safe place, so that is the common point.

segments: Everyone agrees that families need a safe
place, so that is the common point.

Sara
Carlos

hint.es: Lleva ya un sentido negativo: if … not.

pairs: Carlos agrees only if there is a safety plan.

es: Redactar el borrador de una propuesta con tareas, responsables, plazos y una forma de medir el resultado.

teaching.en: A good draft gives each task one person: Ana will order the plants.
teaching.es: Un buen borrador da a cada tarea una persona: Ana pedirá las plantas.
teaching.explanationEs: Draft es el borrador. Will + verbo reparte la tarea y es un compromiso.
segments: A good draft gives each task one
person: Ana will order the plants.
teaching.audioText: A good draft gives each task one person: Ana will order the plants.

teaching.en: Leo is responsible for the budget and will keep all the receipts.
teaching.es: Leo es responsable del presupuesto y guardará todos los recibos.
teaching.explanationEs: Be responsible for + nombre dice quién se encarga; después, will + verbo.
segments: Leo is responsible for the budget
and will keep all the receipts.
teaching.audioText: Leo is responsible for the budget and will keep all the receipts.

teaching.en: The deadline is 14 June, so the volunteers will finish the garden by that date.
teaching.es: El plazo es el 14 de junio, así que los voluntarios terminarán el jardín para esa fecha.
teaching.explanationEs: By + fecha significa a más tardar ese día.
segments: The deadline is 14 June, so the volunteers
will finish the garden by that date.
teaching.audioText: The deadline is 14 June, so the volunteers will finish the garden by that date.

teaching.en: We will count the families who visit the garden every Saturday.
teaching.es: Contaremos las familias que visitan el jardín cada sábado.
teaching.explanationEs: Count es el indicador: algo que se puede contar y repetir.
segments: We will count the families who
visit the garden every Saturday.
teaching.audioText: We will count the families who visit the garden every Saturday.

teaching.en: We will check the result with a weekly count, and it will measure whether more families stay.
teaching.es: Comprobaremos el resultado con un recuento semanal, que medirá si se quedan más familias.
teaching.explanationEs: Check = comprobar. Measure whether + oración dice qué se comprueba.
segments: We will check the result with a weekly count,
and it will measure whether more families stay.
teaching.audioText: We will check the result with a weekly count, and it will measure whether more families stay.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase reparte bien una tarea a una persona?

choices.text: Ana order the plants.
Ana will order the plants.
Ana will to order the plants.

feedback.es: La tarea se reparte con sujeto + will + verbo base. Sin will no hay compromiso y después de will no va to.

hint.es: Busca el compromiso con will y el verbo sin to.

origin.text: Reading Garden. Tasks: order the plants, prepare the soil, count the families. People: Ana, Leo, Mia. Deadline: 14 June.

prompt.es: Completa: «Leo es responsable del presupuesto.»

answer.text: for

feedback.es: En inglés se dice responsible for + nombre, no responsible of.

hint.es: La preposición no es la que usas en español.

hint.es: Es una palabra corta que significa «a más tardar».

prompt.es: Redacta el borrador de la propuesta con los datos de la ficha (90–120 palabras).

answer.text: The problem is that many bikes are broken. For example, sixteen bikes stayed in the school shed last month. So we propose a free repair corner on Saturdays. Sara is responsible for the tools, and she will buy them by 10 August. Carlos will find the volunteers by 1 September. Tom will open the corner by 20 September. Every Saturday, we will count the repaired bikes. This weekly count will measure whether fewer bikes stay in the shed. As a result, more students may ride safely. The team will send a short report after the first month.
accepted: The problem is that many bikes are broken. For example, sixteen bikes stayed in the school shed last month. So we propose a free repair corner on Saturdays. Sara is responsible for the tools, and she will buy them by 10 August. Carlos will find the volunteers by 1 September. Tom will open the corner by 20 September.
